welcomeOnboarding.title: App tour
welcomeOnboarding.subtitle: A short walkthrough of what you can do here and where to click.

guide.kbdHint: Navigate with Left/Right arrows, Home/End; Escape closes the tour.

intro.title: App tour
intro.body: We'll highlight real parts of the screen — the places you'll actually use. Each step says where to click and what opens. Use Next, or close anytime; you can open this tour again from More on the taskbar.

workspace.title: Workspace
workspace.body: The open area is for shortcuts and windows. Click empty space to clear a selection. Right-click empty space for a menu: new shortcuts, widgets, and appearance.

widgets-panel.title: Widgets at hand
widgets-panel.body: This is the mini-widget panel: notes, tasks, favorites. Click a card to open it. Drag to reorder. Keep the panel on the desktop from Settings → Behavior, or press Win+W.
widgets-panel.bodyHidden: The widget panel is hidden — this step shows an example of how it looks.

favorites-widget.title: Favorites
favorites-widget.body: The Favorites card keeps what you open often. Tap Add, enter a title and optional link. One click opens an item.
favorites-widget.bodyHidden: The Favorites card is not on screen — showing an example on the widget panel.

icons.title: Shortcuts
icons.body: Double-click to open an app or file. Right-click for a menu: open, pin, delete. Drag a shortcut to place it.

taskbar.title: Taskbar
taskbar.body: The bar at the bottom is the main starting point. Left: Start and workspaces. Center: pinned apps and open windows. Right: search, notifications, and More.

start.title: Start — all apps
start.body: The EliteEW logo at the bottom left opens Start: the app catalog, recent files, and search. Click an app to open it.

virtual-desktops.title: Workspaces
virtual-desktops.body: The strip next to Start holds separate spaces with their own windows and shortcuts. Click a space to switch, or press Ctrl+Win+Left / Right.

windows.title: Windows and pins
windows.body: The center of the bar holds pinned apps and open-window buttons. Click a button to show that window. Drag a window by its title; at the screen edge it snaps to a half or quarter.

sync-status.title: If saving didn’t work
sync-status.body: Wallpaper, layout, and settings go to the cloud on their own. If a save fails, a chip like this appears above the taskbar. Click Retry. While the cloud is unreachable, those desktop changes stay in this browser.
sync-status.bodyHidden: This chip appears when a save fails — showing an example of how it looks.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.body: The “?” item in More on the taskbar opens the shortcut list: windows, spaces, search. The same window opens with F1. Two useful ones: Win+S for quick search, Ctrl+K for the command palette.

outro.title: You’re ready
outro.body: Start opens an app. Double-click a shortcut to open a file. Widgets and Favorites are for what you use every day. To see this tour again: More on the taskbar → App tour.

nudge.title: App tour
nudge.body: In a couple of minutes we’ll show where to click: apps, files, widgets, and the taskbar.
